Colour TFT Dashboard

Drive a 1.8-inch ST7735 display over SPI and build a compact dashboard while reasoning about bandwidth, colour, and redraw cost.

See ESP32-S3 connectionsStudy the code extract
LevelIntermediate
Suggested time3–4 hours
FocusSPI graphics
DeliverableWorking demonstration

01 · Engineering foundation

Know what the circuit is doing.

Why SPI

A 128 × 160 colour frame contains far more data than a monochrome OLED. A faster SPI clock makes screen updates practical.

Control signals

MOSI and SCK move display data; CS selects the display; DC distinguishes commands from pixel data; RST provides hardware reset.

Redraw strategy

Clearing and repainting the entire display can flicker and waste time. Update only fields that have changed when possible.

02 · Connections

Wire it to the ESP32-S3.

Arrow key: → sent by ESP32-S3 · ← sent by the external device · ↔ bidirectional data · — power, ground, or physical connection

Before applying power

Module power arrangements vary. Confirm whether VDD accepts 3.3 V or 5 V, while keeping all ESP32-S3 logic signals at 3.3 V.

03 · Code focus

Study the important pattern.

#include <Adafruit_GFX.h>
#include <Adafruit_ST7735.h>

Adafruit_ST7735 tft(9, 14, 10); // CS, DC, RST

tft.initR(INITR_BLACKTAB);
tft.setRotation(1);
tft.fillScreen(ST77XX_BLACK);
tft.setTextColor(ST77XX_CYAN);
tft.setCursor(8, 12);
tft.print("Sensor dashboard");

This is an instructional extract, not the complete project. Error handling, library setup, and supporting functions may be omitted deliberately.

04 · Project outcome

What a successful build demonstrates.

  • Identify SPI and display-specific control pins
  • Run a graphics test and select the correct panel initialiser
  • Draw text, shapes, and a changing value
  • Reduce flicker by limiting the redraw area

05 · Diagnose

Use symptoms as evidence.

SymptomFirst checks
White or black screenCheck CS/DC/RST definitions, SPI pins, power, and the panel driver or tab initialiser.
Image shifted or wrong coloursTry the correct initR option and colour-order setting for your panel variant.
Display resets the boardCheck supply current and wiring. Do not assume the board regulator can power every backlight safely.

06 · Extend

Move beyond the first demonstration.

  • PWM backlight dimming
  • Non-blocking gauge animation
  • Display data from an I²C sensor
  • Compare full-screen and partial redraw times

Equipment

What you need

  • ESP32-S3 development board
  • 1.8-inch ST7735 or ST7735S SPI TFT
  • Jumper wires
  • TFT_eSPI or Adafruit ST7735/GFX libraries
  • Suitable external supply if the module load requires it
